claim: PRRX1 was identified as upregulated in IPF through analysis of three curated publicly available transcript microarray databases from NCBI GEO (GDS1252, GDS4279, GDS3951).
source: We screened three curated publicly available transcript microarray databases from NCBI GEO (GDS1252, GDS4279, GDS3951) for transcription factor expression in IPF and control whole lung samples. Among the 210 common genes upregulated at the mRNA level in all three IPF lung datasets compared to their respective control ones (Figure 1A and Supplementary file 1), 12 genes were annotated as transcription factors (Figure 1A) after gene ontology analysis. One of these transcription factors, PRRX1 appeared as an appealing candidate
evidence: The claim is supported by data from three independent microarray datasets showing PRRX1 upregulation in IPF samples.

claim: PRRX1 mRNA generates two proteins by alternative splicing: PRRX1a (216 aa) and PRRX1b (245 aa) that differ at their C-terminal parts.
source: The PRRX1 mRNA generates by alternative splicing two proteins, PRRX1a (216 aa) and PRRX1b (245 aa) that differ at their C-terminal parts.
evidence: This is established knowledge about PRRX1 protein isoforms.

claim: PRRX1a promotes transcriptional activation whereas PRRX1b acts as a transcriptional repressor in mouse cells.
source: Functional in vitro studies suggested that PRRX1a promoted transcriptional activation whereas PRRX1b may act rather as a transcriptional repressor in mouse cells (Norris and Kern, 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to previous work by Norris and Kern, 2001.

claim: Prrx1-/- mice present severe malformation of craniofacial, limb, and vertebral skeletal structures.
source: PRRX1 is essential for fetal development as Prrx1-/- mice present severe malformation of craniofacial, limb, and vertebral skeletal structures (Martin et al., 1995).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Martin et al., 1995.

claim: Prrx1-/- mice display hypoplastic lungs with severe vascularization defects and die soon after birth.
source: Prrx1-/- mice also display hypoplastic lungs with severe vascularization defects and die soon after birth (Ihida-Stansbury et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to Ihida-Stansbury et al., 2004.

claim: Both PRRX1 isoforms (PRRX1a and PRRX1b) were upregulated in Human IPF lungs at the mRNA and protein levels.
source: First, we confirmed that both PRRX1 isoforms were upregulated in Human IPF lungs at the mRNA and protein levels (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A-C including qPCR and western blot analysis.

claim: PRRX1a protein (210 aa) was the main PRRX1 isoform expressed in control and IPF lungs.
source: Immunoblot revealed that PRRX1a protein (210 aa) was the main PRRX1 isoform expressed in control and IPF lungs.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot data showing PRRX1a as the predominant isoform.

claim: PRRX1-positive cells accumulate in IPF compared to control lungs.
source: PRRX1 staining revealed an accumulation of PRRX1-positive cells in IPF compared to control lungs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: PRRX1-positive cells were not detected in the distal alveolar space and in the bronchiolar epithelium of control lung.
source: PRRX1-positive cells were not detected in the distal alveolar space and in the bronchiolar epithelium of control lung (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: PRRX1 nuclear staining was observed in mesenchymal cells (Vimentin-positive but ACTA2 and CD45-negative cells) within peri-vascular and peri-bronchiolar spaces in control lungs.
source: Nevertheless, PRRX1 nuclear staining was observed in mesenchymal cells (Vimentin-positive but ACTA2 and CD45-negative cells) within peri-vascular and peri-bronchiolar spaces (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by double immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: In IPF patients, nuclear PRRX1-positive cells were mainly detected in the fibroblast foci.
source: In IPF patients, nuclear PRRX1-positive cells were mainly detected in the fibroblast foci (also observed by others Yeo et al., 2018) which are the active sites of fibrogenesis (Fernandez and Eickelberg, 2012; Martinez et al., 2017) and in scattered mesenchymal cells within the remodeled / fibrotic lung areas (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1D and citation to Yeo et al., 2018.

claim: PRRX1-positive cells in IPF were all Vimentin positive and CD45 negative but only some were expressing ACTA2.
source: Those PRRX1-positive cells were all Vimentine positive and CD45 negative but only some were expressing ACTA2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by double immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: PRRX1 mRNA expression was restricted to the fibroblast/mesenchymal lung cell lineages in either lung transplant donors or recipients with pulmonary fibrosis.
source: PRRX1 mRNA expression was restricted to the fibroblast / mesenchymal lung cell lineages in either lung transplant donors or recipients with pulmonary fibrosis (Figure 2A–B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell transcriptomic analysis data shown in Figure 2A-B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: In control Human lung, PRRX1 expression was mainly associated with adventitial fibroblasts.
source: In control Human lung, PRRX1 expression was mainly associated with adventitial fibroblasts.
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell transcriptomic analysis.

claim: In IPF, PRRX1 was expressed in fibrosis-associated fibroblast cell populations (HAS1 high and PLIN2 +fibroblasts as well as ACTA2 +myofibroblasts).
source: In IPF, PRRX1 was also expressed in fibrosis-associated fibroblast cell populations (HAS1 high and PLIN2 +fibroblasts as well as ACTA2 +myofibroblasts as defined by Habermann et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell transcriptomic analysis and citation to Habermann et al., 2020.

claim: Both PRRX1 isoforms (PRRX1a and PRRX1b mRNA) were strongly expressed by primary control lung fibroblasts compared to primary alveolar epithelial type 2 cells (AECII) and alveolar macrophages.
source: In vitro, both isoforms, PRRX1a and PRRX1b mRNA were also found to be strongly expressed by primary control lung fibroblasts compared to primary alveolar epithelial type 2 cells (AECII) and alveolar macrophages (Figure 2C) by quantitative PCR (qPCR).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: PRRX1a and -1b levels were increased in IPF primary lung fibroblasts compared to control ones only at the mRNA level.
source: In addition, PRRX1a and –1b levels were increased in IPF primary lung fibroblasts compared to control ones only at the mRNA level as assayed by qPCR and western blot (Figure 2D–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR and western blot data shown in Figure 2D-E.

claim: PRRX1 was detected at the protein level in the nuclei of both control and IPF fibroblasts cultured in vitro.
source: By immunofluorescence, PRRX1 was detected at the protein level in the nuclei of both control and IPF fibroblasts cultured in vitro (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: TGF-β1 treatment (1 ng/ml) was associated with a decrease in the expression level of both PRRX1 isoforms at the mRNA level at 48 hr.
source: 'Transforming growth factor beta 1' (TGF-β1, 1 ng/ml) treatment which triggers myofibroblastic differentiation (Fernandez and Eickelberg, 2012) was associated with a decrease in the expression level of both PRRX1 isoforms at the mRNA level (Figure 3A) at 48 hr.
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3A and citation to Fernandez and Eickelberg, 2012.

claim: PGE2 treatment (100 nM) was associated with an increase of PRRX1 isoforms mRNA and protein in both control and IPF fibroblasts at 48 hr.
source: Conversely, prostaglandin E2 (PGE2, 100 nM) treatment which decreases myofibroblastic differentiation (Fernandez and Eickelberg, 2012) was associated with an increase of PRRX1 isoforms mRNA and protein in both control and IPF fibroblasts (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1) at 48 hr.
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR and western blot data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1, and citation to Fernandez and Eickelberg, 2012.

claim: PRRX1 isoform expression is controlled by a TGF-β/PGE2 balance in lung fibroblasts.
source: These data indicate that PRRX1 isoform expression is controlled by a TGF-β/PGE2 balance in lung fibroblasts.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing opposite effects of TGF-β and PGE2 on PRRX1 expression.

claim: The expression levels of both PRRX1 TFs isoforms mRNA were increased on soft/normal 1.5 kPa stiffness substrate compared to stiff substrates (Glass and 28 kPa culture conditions) in control and IPF fibroblasts.
source: The expression levels of both PRRX1 TFs isoforms mRNA were also increased on soft/normal 1.5 kPa stiffness substrate (Figure 3B) compared to stiff substrates (Glass and 28 kPa culture conditions) in control and IPF fibroblasts.
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Treatment with NS398 (10 µg/ml), a specific PTGS2 inhibitor, abrogated the PRRX1 TFs increase on soft substrate.
source: Treatment with NS398 (10 µg/ml), a specific PTGS2 inhibitor abrogated the PRRX1 TFs increase on soft substrate (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Inhibition of mechanosensitive signalling with Fasudil (35 µM), an inhibitor of ROCK1 and ROCK2, induced PRRX1 TFs mRNA expression in both control and IPF fibroblasts grown on glass/stiff substrate.
source: Conversely, inhibition of mechanosensitive signalling with Fasudil (35 µM), an inhibitor of ROCK1 and ROCK2 (Zhou et al., 2013), induced PRRX1 TFs mRNA expression in both control and IPF fibroblasts grown on glass/stiff substrate (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3C and citation to Zhou et al., 2013.

claim: PRRX1 expression is tightly controlled by extra-cellular matrix stiffness through a PTGS2/ROCK activity balance.
source: Collectively, these data indicate that PRRX1 expression is tightly controlled by extra-cellular matrix stiffness through a PTGS2/ROCK activity balance.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data showing effects of PTGS2 inhibition and ROCK inhibition on PRRX1 expression.

claim: When seeded onto 3D ECM derived from IPF fibroblasts, control fibroblasts showed an upregulation of PRRX1a and -1b TF mRNA expression compared to either plastic culture or control fibroblast derived 3D ECM.
source: When seeded onto 3D ECM derived from IPF fibroblasts, we observed an upregulation of PRRX1a and –1b TF mRNA expression in control fibroblasts compared to either plastic culture or control fibroblast derived 3D ECM.
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data from fibroblast-derived matrix experiments.

claim: PRRX1a and -1b mRNA expression levels were stable in IPF fibroblasts seeded either on control or IPF fibroblast derived 3D ECM compared to plastic culture.
source: Meanwhile, PRRX1a and –1b mRNA expression levels were stable in IPF fibroblasts seeded either on control or IPF fibroblast derived 3D ECM compared to plastic culture (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Both Imatinib (10 µg/ml) and Nintedanib (10 nM) reverted the effect of IPF fibroblast-derived matrix upon PRRX1a and PRRX1b mRNA levels.
source: Both inhibitors reverted the effect of IPF fibroblast-derived matrix upon PRRX1a and PRRX1b mRNA levels (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Treatment with a specific PDGFR inhibitor (PDGFR V) at 10 nM confirmed the PDGFR-dependency of the effect of IPF fibroblast-derived ECM on PRRX1a and -1b mRNA levels in control fibroblasts.
source: Treatment with a specific PDGFR inhibitor (PDGFR V Furuta et al., 2006) at the nanomolar range (10 nM) did confirm the PDGFR-dependency of this effect of IPF fibroblast-derived ECM on PRRX1a and –1b mRNA levels in control fibroblasts (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3E and citation to Furuta et al., 2006.

claim: Knockdown of PRRX1 TFs significantly decreased primary lung fibroblast proliferation in complete growth medium after 72 hr.
source: Knockdown of PRRX1 TFs significantly decreased primary lung fibroblast proliferation in complete growth medium after 72 hr (Figure 4C) as compared to the control siRNA.
evidence: The claim is supported by proliferation assay data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Cell cycle analysis revealed a significant decrease in S phase concomitantly with an increase in G1 phase, suggestive of a G1/S arrest in control and IPF lung fibroblasts treated with PRRX1 siRNA.
source: Cell cycle analysis revealed a significant decrease in S phase concomitantly with an increase in G1 phase, suggestive of a G1/S arrest in control and IPF lung fibroblasts treated with PRRX1 siRNA (Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The potential G1/S arrest was associated with a strong decrease in CCNA2 and CCNE2 mRNA expression after 72 hr.
source: This potential G1/S arrest was also associated with a strong decrease in CCNA2 and CCNE2 mRNA expression after 72 hr (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: PRRX1 inhibition strongly decreased the number of KI67 (MKI67) positive cells in control and IPF lung fibroblasts.
source: PRRX1 inhibition strongly decreased the number of KI67 (MKI67; official name) positive cells in control and IPF lung fibroblasts (Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: An enrichment of PRRX1 binding was observed at the vicinity of PRRX1 response element (PRE) identified in the CCNA2, CCNE2 and MKI67 promoter regions.
source: We observed an enrichment of PRRX1 binding at the vicinity of PRRX1 response element ²(PRE) identified in the CCNA2, CCNE2 and MKI67 promoter regions, suggesting that those genes could be direct PRRX1 TFs target genes.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP data showing PRRX1 binding to these promoter regions.

claim: No PRRX1 binding was detected at the GAPDH transcription starting site (TSS) devoid of PRE.
source: Meanwhile, no PRRX1 binding was detected at the GAPDH transcription starting site (TSS); devoid of PRE (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The inhibition of PRRX1 TFs impacted the upregulation of contractile-associated actin isoforms at the mRNA levels such as ACTA2 (α-SMA) and ACTG2 (γ-SMA) in response to TGF-β1 stimulation.
source: The inhibition of PRRX1 TFs impacted the upregulation of contractile-associated actin isoforms at the mRNA levels such as ACTA2 (α-SMA) and ACTG2 (γ-SMA) in response to TGF-β1 stimulation (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 2)
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: The effect of PRRX1 inhibition upon ACTA2 upregulation was confirmed at the protein level in both control and IPF fibroblasts.
source: The effect of PRRX1 inhibition upon ACTA2 upregulation was confirmed at the protein level in both control and IPF fibroblasts (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Ingenuity Pathway Analysis indicated that the most significantly modulated pathway by PRRX1 inhibition was the TGF-β1 pathway, which was significantly inhibited in TGF-β1-stimulated NHLF treated with PRRX1 siRNA compared to control siRNA.
source: Ingenuity Pathway Analysis at 96 hr indicated that the most significantly modulated pathway by PRRX1 inhibition was the TGF-β1 pathway, which was significantly inhibited in TGF-β1-stimulated NHLF treated with PRRX1 siRNA compared to control siRNA (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 3 and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by whole transcriptome profiling data and pathway analysis shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: PRRX1 knockdown significantly affected the expression of the transmembrane Serine/Threonine kinase receptor TGFBR2.
source: Interestingly, PRRX1 knockdown significantly affected the expression of the transmembrane Serine/Threonine kinase receptor TGFBR2, a key component of the TGF-β pathway (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 3). We confirmed this observation in control and IPF fibroblasts at mRNA and protein levels (Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by transcriptome data and confirmed by qPCR and western blot shown in Figure 5C, 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 3, 4.

claim: PRRX1 knock down inhibited TGF-β1-induced SMAD2 and SMAD3 phosphorylation in control and IPF fibroblasts.
source: In control and IPF fibroblasts, PRRX1 knock down inhibited TGF-β1-induced SMAD2 and SMAD3 phosphorylation (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: PRRX1 knock down did not inhibit the activation of non-canonical/SMAD-independent TGF-β receptor-mediated signaling pathway such as AKT and JNK, in both control and IPF fibroblast.
source: Most importantly, PRRX1 knock down did not inhibit the activation of non-canonical/SMAD-independent TGF-β receptor-mediated signaling pathway such as AKT and JNK, in both control and IPF fibroblast (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data (not shown in figures).

claim: PRRX1 siRNA-mediated inhibition was associated with an increase of PPM1A at both mRNA and protein levels compared to control and IPF fibroblasts treated with control siRNA.
source: We observed that PRRX1 siRNA-mediated inhibition was associated with an increase of PPM1A, a phosphatase member of the PP2C protein family, at both mRNA and protein levels compared to control and IPF fibroblasts treated with control siRNA (Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR and western blot data shown in Figure 5F and Figure 5—figure supplement 4.

claim: siRNA-mediated inhibition of PPM1A partially rescued SMAD3 phosphorylation levels after TGF-β1 stimulation in PRRX1 siRNA-treated control and IPF fibroblasts.
source: In addition, siRNA-mediated inhibition of PPM1A partially rescued SMAD3 phosphorylation levels after TGF-β1 stimulation in PRRX1 siRNA-treated control and IPF fibroblasts (Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4.

claim: An enrichment in PRRX1 TF binding was detected in PPM1A promoter regions.
source: Indeed, we detected an enrichment in PRRX1 TF binding in PPM1A promoter regions (Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4.

claim: Prrx1 complete loss of function inhibited both ACTA2 and COL1 upregulation at both mRNA and protein levels after TGF-β1 stimulation at 1 and 10 ng/ml for 48 hr in Prrx1-/- mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs).
source: In this case, Prrx1 complete loss of function inhibited both ACTA2 and COL1 upregulation at both mRNA and protein levels after TGF-β1 stimulation at 1 and 10 ng/ml for 48 hr (Figure 5—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR and western blot data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5.

claim: Prrx1 loss did not dampen but rather promoted epithelial spheroid formation in a lung spheroid assay.
source: Using wild-type and Prrx1-/- MEFs as stromal cells cultured with wild-type primary mouse lung epithelial cells, we showed that Prrx1 loss did not dampen but rather promoted epithelial spheroid formation (Figure 5—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by lung spheroid assay data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5.

claim: The expression levels of both Prrx1 isoforms mRNA were mainly increased during the fibrotic phase from day 7 to 28 compared to the control saline-treated animals in the bleomycin-induced model of lung fibrosis.
source: In this model, the expression levels of both Prrx1 isoforms mRNA were mainly increased during the fibrotic phase from day 7 to 28 compared to the control saline-treated animals (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: The upregulation of PRRX1 expression level was confirmed at the protein level only from day 14 to 28 during fibrosis phase peak in the bleomycin model.
source: The upregulation of PRRX1 expression level was confirmed at the protein level only from day 14 to 28 during fibrosis phase peak (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: In control mouse lungs, Prrx1 is mainly present in Pi16-positive adventitial and Col15a1 parenchymal 'universal' fibroblast populations.
source: In control lungs, Prrx1 is mainly present in Pi16-positive adventitial and Col15a1 parenchymal 'universal' fibroblast populations (Buechler et al., 2021), which also express Col14a1 (see Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1 and citation to Buechler et al., 2021.

claim: Prrx1 is detected in the fibrosis-associated Lrrc15/Cthrc1-positive fibroblast population producing the highest levels of ECM proteins in animals treated with bleomycin.
source: Interestingly, Prrx1 is also detected in the fibrosis-associated Lrrc15/Cthrc1-positive fibroblast population producing the highest levels of ECM proteins (Tsukui et al., 2020) in animals treated with bleomycin, as shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1 and citation to Tsukui et al., 2020.

claim: The loss of one Prrx1 allele was not associated with any haploinsufficiency and Prrx1+/- mice were not protected from lung fibrosis at day 14 after intratracheal instillation of bleomycin.
source: We observed that the loss of one Prrx1 allele was not associated with any haploinsufficiency (Figure 6—figure supplement 2) and those Prrx1+/- +/- mice were not protected from lung fibrosis at day 14 after intratracheal instillation of bleomycin (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR, western blot, and histological data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Prrx1 ASO strongly reduced the expression of both Prrx1 isoforms at the mRNA and protein levels compared to control ASO in the bleomycin model.
source: As compared to control ASO, Prrx1 ASO strongly reduced the expression of both Prrx1 isoforms at the mRNA and protein levels (Figure 6A–B)
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR and western blot data shown in Figure 6A-B.

claim: Prrx1 ASO reduced the extent of lung lesions on day 14 in the bleomycin model.
source: As compared to control ASO, Prrx1 ASO strongly reduced the expression of both Prrx1 isoforms at the mRNA and protein levels (Figure 6A–B) and reduced the extent of lung lesions on day 14 (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by histological injury score data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Lung collagen content was decreased in Prrx1 ASO-treated animals as assessed with picrosirius staining, immunohistochemistry and hydroxyproline assay.
source: Lung collagen content was decreased as assessed with picrosirius staining, immunohistochemistry and hydroxyproline assay (Figure 6D–F).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple assays shown in Figure 6D-F.

claim: A decrease in ACTA2 staining was observed in Prrx1 ASO-treated animals at day 14 by immunohistochemistry.
source: A similar decrease in ACTA2 staining was observed in Prrx1 ASO-treated animals at day 14 by immunohistochemistry (Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6E and Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: Prrx1 ASO treatment dampened the accumulation of PDGFR-positive mesenchymal cells in bleomycin-treated animals compared to the control ASO bleomycin group at day 14.
source: Prrx1 ASO treatment also dampened the accumulation of PDGFR-positive mesenchymal cells in bleomycin-treated animals compared to the control ASO bleomycin group at day 14 by immunohistochemistry (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: Prrx1 ASO decreased Col1a1, Fn1 and Acta2 mRNA content in PRRX1 ASO-treated bleomycin mice compared to control ASO-treated ones.
source: In addition, Prrx1 ASO decreased Col1a1, Fn1 and Acta2 mRNA content (Figure 7A) in PRRX1 ASO-treated bleomycin mice compared to control ASO-treated ones.
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The expression levels of COL1, FN1 and ACTA2 were decreased at the protein level in Prrx1 ASO-treated bleomycin mice.
source: Finally, the expression levels of COL1, FN1 and ACTA2 were also decreased at the protein level as assayed by western blot (Figure 7B–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 7B-C.

claim: The dampened fibrosis development observed in PRRX1 ASO-treated bleomycin mice was associated with a decrease in key fibrosis mediators such as Tgfb1 and Ctgf as well as inflammatory markers as Tnf and Serpin-1 at the mRNA level.
source: The dampened fibrosis development observed in PRRX1 ASO-treated bleomycin mice was also associated with a decrease in key fibrosis mediators such as Tgfb1 and Ctgf as well as inflammatory markers as Tnf and Serpin-1 at the mRNA level (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: The expression of Col14a1 mRNA was strongly decreased in the Prrx1 ASO-treated animals compared to control ASO at day 14.
source: Interestingly, the expression of Col14a1 mRNA was also strongly decreased in the Prrx1 ASO-treated animals compared to control ASO at day 14 as assayed by qPCR (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: Eln and Tnc mRNA levels were decreased in the Prrx1 ASO-treated bleomycin group.
source: With respect to another fibrosis-associated key ECM protein, Eln and Tnc mRNA levels were also decreased in the Prrx1 ASO-treated bleomycin group (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: The expression levels of the proliferation marker Mki67 was decreased at the mRNA levels in the Prrx1 ASO-treated animals compared to control ASO at day 14.
source: The expression levels of the proliferation marker Mki67 was decreased at the mRNA levels in the Prrx1 ASO-treated animals compared to control ASO at day 14 as assayed by qPCR (Figure 7D).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: An overall decrease in KI67-positive cells was observed by immunochemistry in the Prrx1 ASO-treated animal lungs after bleomycin challenge compared to control ASO ones at day 14.
source: An overall decrease in KI67-positive cells was also observed by immunochemistry in the Prrx1 ASO-treated animal lungs after bleomycin challenge compared to control ASO ones at day 14 (Figure 7D).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The decrease in KI67 positivity was confirmed in mesenchymal PDGFR-positive cells after performing PDGFR KI67 double staining in the Prrx1 ASO-treated animals compared to control ASO at day 14.
source: Such decrease in KI67 positivity was also confirmed in mesenchymal PDGFR-positive cells after performing PDGFR KI67 double staining in the Prrx1 ASO-treated animals compared to control ASO at day 14 (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by double immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: The effects of Prrx1 inhibition during late fibrosis phase (day 21-28) were less potent as measured by hydroxyproline content.
source: In this case, the effects of Prrx1 inhibition during late fibrosis phase were less potent as measured by hydroxyproline content, even though the injury score, accumulation of PDGFR-positive cells by immunohistochemistry, protein levels of COL1 and FN1 by immunoblots were still decreased in Prrx1 ASO-treated animals compared to control ASO after bleomycin insult at day 28 (see Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple assays shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: In basal condition, Prrx1 knock down was associated with a decrease in Acta2 mRNA expression in mouse PCLS.
source: In basal condition, Prrx1 knock down was associated with a decrease in Acta2 mRNA expression in mouse PCLS (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: A decreased expression of ACTA2, COL1A1 and FN1 mRNA was observed in three IPF PCLS treated with PRRX1 ASO compared to control ASO-treated ones.
source: However, we observed a decreased expression of ACTA2, COL1A1 and FN1 mRNA in three IPF PCLS treated with PRRX1 ASO compared to control ASO-treated ones (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: In both mouse and Human PCLS, ACTA2, COL1A1, and FN1 mRNA upregulation was lessened in FC-stimulated PCLS with PRRX1 ASO compared to control.
source: In both mouse and Human PCLS, ACTA2, COL1A1, and FN1 mRNA upregulation was lessened in FC-stimulated PCLS with PRRX1 ASO compared to control (Figure 8).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 8.

claim: ACTA2 and COL1 protein levels were decreased in FC-stimulated mouse PCLS treated with PRRX1 ASO.
source: We confirmed those findings at the protein levels for ACTA2 and COL1 by western blot in mouse PCLS (Figure 8).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 8.

claim: In Human PCLS stimulated with FC, PRRX1 ASO treatment was associated with a decreased Collagen accumulation compared to control ASO.
source: In Human PCLS stimulated with FC, morphological analysis revealed that PRRX1 ASO treatment was associated with a decreased Collagen accumulation compared to control ASO (Figure 8).
evidence: The claim is supported by picrosirius staining data shown in Figure 8.

claim: PRRX1 TFs are upregulated in mesenchymal cells accumulating in the fibrotic areas of IPF lungs.
source: Our results demonstrate that (1) PRRX1 TFs are upregulated in mesenchymal cells accumulating in the fibrotic areas of IPF lungs
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by multiple pieces of data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: The expression of PRRX1 TFs is positively regulated by cues associated with an undifferentiated phenotype in control and IPF primary lung fibroblasts.
source: (2) the expression of PRRX1 TFs is positively regulated by cues associated with an undifferentiated phenotype in control and IPF primary lung fibroblasts
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by multiple pieces of data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: PRRX1 TFs are required for proliferation as well as proper myofibroblastic differentiation in vitro.
source: (3) PRRX1 TFs are required for proliferation as well as proper myofibroblastic differentiation in vitro (see Figure 9 for summary).
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by multiple pieces of data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Inhibition of Prrx1 with LNA-modified ASO strongly impacted lung fibrosis development in in vivo and ex vivo preclinical models.
source: Finally, inhibition of Prrx1 with LNA-modified ASO strongly impacted lung fibrosis development in in vivo and ex vivo preclinical models.
evidence: This is a summary claim supported by multiple pieces of data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: IPF results from progressive alterations of alveolar epithelial cells leading to the recruitment of mesenchymal cells to the alveolar regions of the lung with secondary deposition of extracellular matrix, and destruction of the normal lung structure and physiology.
source: According to the current paradigm, IPF results from progressive alterations of alveolar epithelial cells leading to the recruitment of mesenchymal cells to the alveolar regions of the lung with secondary deposition of extracellular matrix, and destruction of the normal lung structure and physiology.
evidence: This represents established knowledge about IPF pathogenesis.

claim: IPF develops in a susceptible, aging individual and is promoted by interaction with environmental agents such as inhaled particles, tobacco smoke, inhaled pollutants, viral and bacterial agents.
source: IPF develops in a susceptible, aging individual and is promoted by interaction with environmental agents such as inhaled particles, tobacco smoke, inhaled pollutants, viral and bacterial agents (Froidure et al., 2020; Martinez et al., 2017).
evidence: This represents established knowledge about IPF risk factors, supported by citations.

claim: Cells of mesenchymal origin such as fibroblasts are the main cellular components responsible for tissue remodeling during normal and pathological lung tissue repair.
source: Among the multifaceted tissue cellular 'ecosystem', cells of mesenchymal origin such as fibroblasts are the main cellular components responsible for tissue remodeling during normal and pathological lung tissue repair (Fernandez and Eickelberg, 2012; Martinez et al., 2017).
evidence: This represents established knowledge about fibroblast function, supported by citations.
